payload.title: omp-guard-precise and purview-guard-precise built off plan/purview-routes, not line(guard-precision)
payload.body: Ruled by the planner of guard-precision: the line takes plan/purview-routes as its base, once; neither unit is rebuilt. Both units' specs already require their branch to hold cbac6a5f (their BASE clause), because purview-routes changes their files over main (packages/forge/src/adapters/omp/render.ts and omp.test.ts; the purview guardrail cell, targets and test), and bind cut plan/guard-precision at main 15d0a621 without it. So, before merging omp-guard-precise or purview-guard-precise onto the line, the integrator merges plan/purview-routes (cbac6a5f, closed and whole) into plan/guard-precision in one commit, e.g. 'chore(guard-precision): take plan/purview-routes as base', then merges each achieved unit as usual. Why this is safe: purview-routes is released (PR #42) before guard-precision in any case, and main takes PRs as merge commits (#39, #40), so once #42 lands main holds cbac6a5f and guard-precision's promotion carries only its own work; purview-routes' records on the line are the same files main will then hold. Checked at plan/guard-precision 2ce806e4: git merge-tree of the line with plan/purview-routes is clean, and of that result with unit/omp-guard-precise (79e6f36c) is clean. Promotion order: guard-precision's pull request is opened only after PR #42 is merged; if #42 is instead squash-merged, the line is merged with main after it before promotion. A unit's 'git diff --name-only <base holding cbac6a5f> <landed>' criterion is read against cbac6a5f, not the line's cut.
